AES.why: Independent power producer and utility owner signing renewable and storage PPAs directly with data center customers (8.2 GW of data center PPAs, 4.2 GW operating and 4 GW in backlog) plus 2.1 GW of signed data center agreements at AES Ohio.
AES.evidence: AES Q3 FY2025 (11-05-2025), CEO Andres Gluski: 'We're also benefiting from the completion of projects serving data centers that we have signed over the last few years. Of 8.2 gigawatts, 4.2 gigawatts are in operation and 4 gigawatts are in our backlog.'
AES.approved: user pre-approved 2026-10-01 (enrich_waitlist.json, user ruling: add AES despite the earlier do-not-add)

players.product: Renewable and battery storage PPAs for data center customers (8.2 GW signed: 4.2 GW operating, 4 GW backlog), powered-land data center sites with PPAs, and utility service for data center load at AES Ohio and AES Indiana

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2025 adjusted EBITDA of $830 million versus $698 million a year ago, driven by new renewables projects, utility rate base investment and cost savings; adjusted EPS $0.75 versus $0.71. Renewables EBITDA up 46% year-to-date, which the CFO said will likely be around 50% by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: adj EBITDA $830 million (vs $698 million); adj EPS $0.75 (vs $0.71); renewables EBITDA +46% YTD

quarterly_data.signal: Reaffirmed 2025 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $2.65 billion to $2.85 billion and adjusted EPS guidance of $2.10 to $2.26; reaffirmed 5% to 7% long-term adjusted EBITDA growth through 2027, with the growth rate increasing to the low teens next year; an incremental $400 million of run-rate EBITDA expected beyond 2027 from backlog projects; $300 million annual cost-savings run rate in 2026; CFO expects to extend guidance out to 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 adj EBITDA $2.65 billion to $2.85 billion; adj EPS $2.10 to $2.26; +$400 million run-rate EBITDA beyond 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Data center PPAs: of 8.2 GW signed with data centers, 4.2 GW are in operation and 4 GW in backlog, nearly half of which is under construction and will be added in the next 18 months (excludes utility data center business). PPAs signed year-to-date total 2.2 GW, of which 1.6 GW with data centers; CEO confident of signing 4 GW of new PPAs this year (at least 1.8 GW more in advanced negotiations). CFO: data center PPA returns tend to be at the higher end of the 12% to 15% range because time to power is extremely important. AES Ohio has 2.1 GW of signed data center agreements; at AES Indiana deals are expected in the 1.5 to 2.5 GW range, to be announced in the next couple of months.
quarterly_data.figure: 8.2 GW data center PPAs (4.2 GW operating, 4 GW backlog); 2.2 GW signed YTD; AES Ohio 2.1 GW

quarterly_data.signal: Signed a development transfer agreement (DTA) with a large data center customer to provide powered land for a data center site adjacent to two AES power projects, with an ongoing PPA; CEO: AES's first DTA involving the transfer of a data center site, a co-located opportunity interconnected with the grid and renewables, to be announced jointly with the customer.

Construction and backlog: on schedule to complete 3.2 GW of construction this year (2.9 GW completed year-to-date); another 4.8 GW of the 11.1 GW backlog under construction through 2027; repowering 1.2 GW of natural gas at AES Indiana, operational next year. The 7.5 GW U.S. backlog is entirely safe-harbored, with 4 GW more safe-harbored in the pipeline and line of sight to another 3 to 4 GW before July 4, 2026, enabling tax-credit projects through 2030. CEO: AES had on-site or in-country everything needed for this year and next, and from 2026 relies on domestically produced key inputs.
quarterly_data.figure: 11.1 GW backlog; 4.8 GW under construction; 7.5 GW U.S. backlog safe-harbored

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on demand: very strong interest from data center and corporate customers, focused on time to power; this year probably 90% of what meets demand is renewables and batteries; more than half of AES solar projects now come with batteries, and AES sees demand for behind-the-meter storage at data centers themselves. CEO does not see cannibalization from hyperscaler behind-the-meter procurement.

Utilities: AES Indiana partial rate settlement (revenue increase cut by $105 million, final order expected Q2 2026) and IRP filed with scenarios of 520 MW to 2.5 GW of new data center load; Pike County 200 MW storage project online (largest in MISO) and 295 MW more capacity by year-end. AES Ohio distribution settlement with an annual revenue increase of approximately $168 million; transmission expected to be 40% of AES Ohio rate base by 2027; utility rate base growth guided at roughly 11%.
quarterly_data.figure: AES Ohio 2.1 GW signed; Indiana IRP 520 MW to 2.5 GW; ~11% rate base growth
